subject.title: [Bug]: read tool drops memory/ prefix in multi-agent setup, causing ENOENT

question: Should maintainers accept the open PR's scoped ENOENT-only daily-memory fallback in the read tool, or require the prefix-loss fix to move upstream into startup or prompt routing?
rationale: Current main still fails the bare-date read shape, but the candidate fix changes read-tool resolution semantics and must preserve the workspace sandbox boundary.

options.title: Accept the scoped fallback
options.body: Land the linked PR if normal merge checks stay clean and the synthesized retry remains ENOENT-only and sandbox-guarded.

options.title: Require an upstream prefix fix
options.body: Ask the PR to move the fix to the startup or prompt path if maintainers do not want the read tool to infer daily-memory paths.

options.title: Reject the fallback
options.body: Close the linked PR and keep this issue open only if maintainers decide bare-date reads should continue to fail at the workspace root.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped fallback
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR if normal merge checks stay clean and the synthesized retry remains ENOENT-only and sandbox-guarded.

likelyOwner.reason: The open decision centers on the agent read-tool boundary where recent read-wrapper history points most strongly to this owner.
